text:
maya: FYI — Customer 'BrightApps' in us-west reported repeated SSE disconnects this morning. They see partial chunks sometimes, then a 502 and immediate reconnect loop. Billing spike + customer panic. Anyone on this? :grimacing:

sam: on it. do we have a request id or trace?

maya: trace id 7643f2b9. Customer captured a client-side log showing 'socket write returned EAGAIN' and repeated HTTP reconnects every ~2s. They claim server aborts after ~15s of attempts.

alex: EAGAIN on write usually indicates slow consumer / send buffer full. Could be client not reading fast enough or proxy queuing. Any proxy between client and our sidecar?

maya: they're on a managed mobile client behind a corporate proxy. Also using HTTP/2 from app -> LB -> our sidecar.

nithin: pinging eng-oncall infra here. @infra-bot can you pull recent sidecar logs for trace 7643f2b9 and show socket-level errors?

infra-bot: logs fetched for trace 7643f2b9 (tail):
```
[2026-02-14T09:12:20Z] conn=abcd write=1024 err=EAGAIN
[2026-02-14T09:12:22Z] conn=abcd write=0 err=EPIPE
[2026-02-14T09:12:22Z] conn=abcd aborting stream due to persistent write failure
[2026-02-14T09:12:22Z] stream=7643f2b9 status=502 reason=stream-abort
```

sam: that pattern matches backpressure leading to abort. We close the stream to protect worker memory. But the reconnect loop could cause billing churn if we count partial output or reconnect metadata.

alex: hypothesis: client is a slow consumer (mobile UI) + corporate proxy buffering / head-of-line blocking. The sidecar attempts to write chunked frames, socket blocks (EAGAIN), then subsequent 0-byte write/EPIPE when peer closed. Sidecar aborts per our write-retry policy.

maya: customer provided a minimal repro using curl from a VM in their network that reproduces ~50% disconnects. They said increasing client read window helps.

nithin: mitigation options: 1) increase write-retry attempts or backoff window on sidecar for that tenant (temp), 2) enable smaller chunk sizes and more frequent flushes to avoid large writes filling send buffer, 3) advise customer to tune proxy + app read loop, 4) implement a reconnect-debounce on client to reduce billing loops.

sam: for quick repro we asked customer to run:
```
curl -v --no-buffer \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?trace=7643f2b9' | pv -qL 10 > /dev/null
```
This simulates a 10 bytes/sec consumer and reproduces EAGAIN within ~10-20s.

alex: good repro. For diagnostics ask them to run netstat / ss during repro and capture tcp_info (snd_cwnd, rmem/sndbuf usage). Also check LB idle/timeouts and HTTP/2 SETTINGS initial_window_size.

maya: customer asked if disabling chunked responses or switching to polling would avoid charges. can we confirm billing behavior?

nithin: partial execution currently counts as billable tokens when the stream is accepted and response generation occurs server-side. Reconnects that trigger new responses will be billed separately. If we abort mid-response due to write errors, tokens already generated are billed. So yes, their reconnect loop could spike costs.

sam: action items: 1) support: advise customer to add client-side exponential reconnect backoff and increase read buffer. 2) infra: collect sidecar kernel/socket metrics for that tenant (sndbuf fill, write-block seconds) and LB config for that route. 3) eng-runtime: consider a tenant-scoped tweak for write retry/backoff + smaller default chunk writes as a hotfix. 4) billing: flag spikes for potential credit review if customer follows remediation steps.

alex: I'll draft a short workaround doc for them: set client read loop to drain events, increase socket rcvbuf, reduce client-side processing per chunk, and enable a 5s base reconnect backoff.

maya: sending customer the curl repro and suggested steps now. I'll escalate to eng-runtime if we see repeated incidents after workstation-level changes. :thumbsup:

nithin: thanks all. tagging this with high-priority support case. If anyone finds a config knob that can be flipped without a deploy, drop it here.

sam: one more note — add a metric for 'write-block-duration' per connection in the sidecar; it'll help us catch slow-consumer tenants proactively. :eyes:
